records.text: What is the Tide Ledger?
Linked gates, local signals, a central chart drum. It moves water between connected channels. Sailors gave it the rest of the ocean in the telling.
Was Vane there when the relief boat stranded?
Not in the work I saw. Don't put a familiar face into an old gap. The record should still say who signed what.
Why keep the chart?
First to keep it from another confident operator. Later because returning it meant explaining why I'd hidden it. The second reason lasted longer.
How do we reach the installation?
The service landing, not the company approach. Here is my tracing. Check it against today's board; old ink doesn't know today's water.
Are you coming?
I'll stay where stranded crews can find a door. You need someone to hear you when you return, not everyone in one boat.
I'm angry with you.
You may be. You don't have to make me comfortable before we do something useful.
We'll need more than your account.
Yes. Ask the caretaker for the operating record. His name is Bram. Ask what he needs before deciding what he knows.
I'll take the tracing.
It's on the bar. Keep the original survey with it. One shows the entrance; the other gives you something to check.
Will you keep watch together?
I will keep this approach open.
I will keep the departure entry and take messages. Partner, not equipment.
Agreed.
Can you stop the company?
Not by standing here more magnificently.
But a clear landing and an accurate message are available within our budget.
What if we're late?
We tell Mara and keep the approach clear. We do not improvise a gate setting.
Does their charter let them close everything?
I'll read the whole charter before answering that. A clause without its neighbours is a dangerous pet.
Another duel?
Not while you're asking for useful work. I am trying not to spoil the novelty.
Will you take me to Bellweather?
Yes. We have a service route to check, and people ashore to tell. I would prefer not to become a second unexplained absence.
Check my departure plan.
Put today's board, the fixed marks and the tracing together. I'll check your conclusion, not supply it.
West approach, fixed transit, today's ebb. I agree with what you've checked.
Who owns the boat now?
I do. You have my passage and my help. It is useful to say these things before someone starts naming the cabin.
Can we leave right now?
What will you do at the shoal?
Mind the berth and the return route. You investigate. If the instructions disagree with me, bring the instructions.
Will you wait here?
Yes. No unexplained departures. It is becoming a professional principle.
The centre can't simply be stopped.
Then find out what takes its place.
A navigator likes a second route before the first disappears.
Take me back.
Whenever you're ready. The service berth will still be here if we return.
What does the central drum actually do?
Times and coordinates gate commands. It doesn't contain the tide. The gates still need agreed instructions when the centre stops sending them.
Why not break it?
Because a stopped instruction isn't a safe instruction. Local stations must accept control together first.
Mara told me about the relief boat.
The incident binder is here. Read it beside what she remembers. An admission and a record should help each other, not replace each other.
Do you have the company's operating record?
Commands, acknowledgements and settings. The duplicate recorder's collar leaks; its copies blur. Its service tray is separate from the live drive. We can repair the copy path without touching a gate.
Who ordered the old relief-run change?
The old duty sheet names its operator. It isn't a Vane order. Today's entries have their own authorisation marks. Keep the years apart.
Can the local stations take over?
There is a documented procedure. Read it at the overlook, then try the disconnected board. If you understand the copy, we can discuss the original.
Can you do this for me?
I can service the apparatus. I can't decide what your evidence proves, or prepare people I haven't spoken to.
Why did nobody listen?
A machine that works looks as though nobody did anything. I have filed several very uneventful reports.
What should I take?
A legible record, the procedure, and your questions. Leave the gates, the originals and my kettle.
I have a clear operating copy.
Read what it records before deciding what it proves.
Keep the source marks attached. A useful page shouldn't lose its address.
The model worked.
Good. The harbour still needs current measurements, working local controls and people who have agreed to use them.
Can you open the command floor?
Not under the present lock. The inspection bypass is reached by the service route, but using it safely requires local cover. Access and readiness are different problems.
Will you help when we return?
I'll keep the record and service access in order. Tell me when the local stations are actually ready. Not when someone hopes they are.
What still needs proving?
Which settings changed, who could pass, and what they were charged. I can give you the first. The harbour must supply the others.
We're going to the shoal.
I can print a departure notice without predicting the return. That is an editorial improvement.
Don't call it a treasure hunt.
What should I call it?
An inspection.
I shall need a larger typeface.
Can you publish Mara's account?
With her agreement and the documents beside it. A confession isn't a licence to stop checking.
Here is a verified operating copy.
I'll keep the source with it. We still need the access notices and fees before the headline can claim the whole story.
Mara maintained your family's system.
Then she knows where the drawings meet the weather. I should have asked her sooner.
How can local readings agree if their levels differ?
Agree on the watch and the map, not on being identical. Different basins can have different levels at the same time.
Can I reuse my middle inlet reading?
As a dated observation, yes. As tomorrow's water, no. A measurement expires as an instruction before it expires as evidence.
The model shows local control can work.
Then we prepare the real stations. A successful model is a reason to work carefully, not to stop checking.
I'm inspecting the shoal.
The public inspection route remains available. The command floor does not. Bring your questions to the appropriate side of the rail.
Why secure the centre?
Because conflicting instructions do not become safer by being sincerely given.
Neither does one instruction become right by being the only one allowed.
Your name is on the pending dispatch request.
Yes. I have been quite public about coordinated passage.
Coordinated and exclusive aren't the same word.
We continue to disagree about their practical separation.
Will you stop the order?
Not on the basis of an objection without a workable alternative.
The historical record supports your account.
Keep it with the account. Neither needs to stand alone.
We must prepare the local stations.
Then tell us what is needed. This time we decide with the information on the table.
We have the operating record.
Keep the sequence numbers. I dislike documents that arrive without their neighbours.
I will continue guarding the neighbours.
I gave Vane a working copy. She paid me. Now my correction is on the route she means to sell back to everyone.
Did she change your measurements?
No. I wanted the work to count. I didn't ask hard enough who it would count for.
Then I owe you the part I left out.
You recognised the chart.
I helped maintain the Tide Ledger. That was one of our service surveys.
Years ago, an operator tried to run more channels from the centre. We changed a gate before the receiving station had confirmed its level.
What happened?
A relief boat sat on the mud until the next safe tide. Nobody died. People waiting for supplies still went without them.
I had a doubtful reading. I let certainty outrank it. Afterwards I kept the chart where nobody could use it.
Until you gave it to me without telling me why it mattered.
I thought you would ask the questions I had stopped asking. I made that choice for you. I'm sorry.
I should have read what I was agreeing to, not what I hoped it meant.
Yes. And you should have had the history. Both things can be true.
Then let's stop leaving parts out.
There is a service landing at Bellweather. I'll put the tracing here. Check today's water, and tell someone where you're going.
A route, a check, and someone who knows to ask. That's a better beginning.
We're going to the shoal. I need someone here who knows our route and will keep the landing clear.
At last. A command appropriate to my stature.
A request. With two names on the answer.
Quibble and Fine Print. Harbour watch. Both responsible, both credited.
West service approach. Fixed transit. Today's ebb, not yesterday's sheltered basin.
Now the old route and the present water have had an introduction.
Transit steady. West service approach.
That arch looks less like a treasure entrance from this side.
There is a sign.
‘Caretakers: mind the second step.’
An unusually considerate curse.
Someone gave a public works station the manners of an ancient warning.
People read warnings more carefully when they look expensive.
They left a dry walkway. I like the practical part.
Visitor or replacement caretaker?
Visitor. Nell. Mara said I should ask what you need.
Someone to read the labels before touching the things beneath them.
I can begin immediately.
Then you're already ahead of the last inspection.
The company is using this station to make one paid route the dependable one. I need to know how to stop that without wrecking the harbour.
Good. Most people shorten that question in the dangerous place.
The relief boat was stranded after a change without a receiving acknowledgement. That supports Mara's account.
It doesn't make the old operator and today's company the same people.
Two tabs. Blue triangle. A replaceable collar.
Six in a box. Seven, if the supplier has had a good morning.
And the crown?
The cover is old. The catalogue is more useful.
Clear marks. Original untouched.
A treasure I can leave here and still take with me.
A command, a calibration and a pending order. Enough to follow. Not permission to invent the rest.
If that stops sending orders, does everything stop safely?
No. Water keeps arriving. Gates need a coordinated setting, not an absent supervisor.
So breaking it would leave the problem in charge.
Now read the alternative.
Same watch. Each local level. Every station ready before the centre lets go.
The machine was built to be maintained by people who could talk to one another.
We have been rather slow to service that part.
Could this be the relic the pedestal deserves?
Only if you write its part number.
Lint. One pocket. Unverified antiquity.
Put it back. We've only just made the records legible.
We don't need a bigger way to break the centre. We need the local stations ready to stop depending on it.
And a record of why you're doing it.
Current readings. Named people. The operating copy beside the access notices.
That sounds less like an adventure.
It sounds like one we might bring everyone home from.
What did you find?
Instructions. And the reason nobody should carry them alone.
Where first?
Home. We have people to ask, not orders to give.
West approach, fixed transit, today’s ebb. I agree with what you’ve checked.
Put today’s board, the fixed marks and the tracing together. I’ll check your conclusion, not supply it.
Keep the source marks attached. A useful page shouldn’t lose its address.
The copy path needs a seal, not a weather system.
That belongs with my evidence, not inside this mechanism.
Mara’s tracing stays beside my original survey. Today’s water still needs checking.
The original stays here. I can keep the information in my notebook.
No live changes. Use the marked inspection route and prepare local cover first.
The copy records commands, my calibration source and a pending order. It does not prove every accusation.
She has made room at the bar. Not an escape route.
A maintenance entrance, a landing, and Mara’s initials. No treasure crosses.
The chart was in here. Its history wasn’t.
Two names, one job. Quibble and Fine Print must both agree.
TODAY’S DEPARTURE WATCH: EBB. WEST SERVICE APPROACH. EAST ARM CLOSED FOR COMPANY TRIALS.
The warehouse corner and lighthouse notch still form the outer transit.
The float and the loose leaves both run west. This agrees with today’s board.
Compare Mara’s tracing, the original survey and today’s observations.
Second Opinion remains his boat. We sail with his consent.
Three blue stripes, copper kettle, safely afloat.
Old ink does not know today’s water.
Safely open, with its crank where it belongs. No need to repeat a solved problem.
TIDE LEDGER. LOCAL CHANNEL WORKS. INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE ACCESS.
INSPECTION GALLERY: RAISED WALKWAY. DO NOT ENTER THE WET STAIR. REPORT TO CARETAKER.
Wet steps, no inspection marking. The dry path is already offering itself.
No unexplained departures. He will wait at the berth.
Transport isn’t a pocket-sized arrangement.
A caretaker, not a keeper of curses.
CENTRAL DRUM: COMMAND COORDINATION. LOCAL GATES: WATER ROUTING. RECORDER: COPY OF COMMANDS AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS. TRAINING BOARD: NO GATE CONNECTION.
RELIEF RUN: receiving level unconfirmed; central change issued; service boat grounded until safe water returned; supplies delayed; no deaths recorded. The old operator is not Vane.
Unlike the household version, this one has no opinion about the table.
DUPLICATE RECORDER COLLAR. TWO TABS. BLUE TRIANGLE. SERVICE PART, NOT CONTROL EQUIPMENT.
The copy path is separate from the live drive. SERVICE releases its dry tray.
That is connected to gates. This bench is not. The distinction is usefully large.
An empty recess beneath the Crown of the Faithful Record. The catalogue is more useful.
A schedule turning into instructions. Not the source of the water. No live shutdown without local cover.
LOCAL COVER → ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS → CENTRAL ISOLATION → LOCAL RUN. REVERSE ONLY BY DOCUMENTED HANDOVER.
DISCONNECTED MODEL. SAMPLE WATCH C. NOT VALID FOR LIVE OPERATIONS.
COMPANY OPERATION AREA. PUBLIC INSPECTION ABOVE. Access and readiness are different problems.
Rook’s name identified the mechanism. It didn’t identify every decision made with it.
My correction, their dispatch policy. Both still on the page.
Warm tea, parked table, a bell waiting for a person. A small working example.
The trolley is safely parked. The workshop passage stays open.
The occupants and reservations have reached a temporary understanding.
Inspection remains public. Operating policy remains with the director. The gap between them is getting crowded.
Quiet coastal public works station on a rocky shoal, gentle water lapping stone, distant soft brass clockwork and sea breeze. No voices no music. Seamless loop.
